reason: While the passage opens with Moses as a working person (shepherd tending flocks), the narrative perspective quickly transcends that of regular people. The overwhelming majority of the text consists of divine revelation and God's speech to Moses, focusing on transcendent spiritual matters (God's self-identification, divine names, cosmic promises) rather than maintaining the perspective of an ordinary working person navigating daily labor or secular concerns. The perspective shifts from the mundane (shepherding) to the supernatural and prophetic.
